rationale: PINS the receiver-type channel and its EVIDENCE classes (2026-10-18 contract): `metadata.owner` is the EXISTING authoritative store channel (member-owner-resolution.ts's claimOwnerCarryingTargets + resolveMemberTargetsByOwner, read by both resolution paths in parallel-indexer.ts) and `metadata.ownerEvidence` says which syntactic proof produced it. Four proofs, all syntactic: (1) new — `const fresh = new Service(); fresh.run()`; (2) assignment — `this.svc = new Service(); this.svc.run()` AND the class field `svc = new Service(); this.svc.run()`; (3) this — `this.helper()` inside `class Consumer` (positional: the enclosing class DECLARATION, the only shape that publishes a class-like symbol for the owner channel); (4) jsdoc — `/** @type {Service} */ const documented = build(); documented.run()` AND the constructor parameter form `/** @param {Service} dep */ constructor(dep){ this.dep = dep } ; this.dep.run()`. CONTROLS: `controlResult`'s `result.run()` has a call initialiser and no JSDoc, so no owner may be attached; `controlDynamicThis`'s `this.other()` is a plain function's dynamic `this`, not a class instance, so no owner may be attached. The coverage this fixture pins is METADATA; it makes no resolution claim — the arbiter resolves targets, not owners, and the count of owner-carrying rows is reported separately by evidence class.
